overview: This bundle consists of Department of State lists of papers and cross-reference sheets concerning aerial navigation in Japan, chiefly during the 1930s. The principal index surveys Japanese civil aviation, pilot training, aircraft manufacture, aerial beacons and air-defense planning, the expansion of routes to China, Korea, Taiwan, Sakhalin, Southeast Asia and the South Seas Mandate, and the increasing consolidation of air transport under government control. A separate jacket-case index traces Ford Motor Company’s 1930 shipment of an airplane to Yokohama for demonstration flights in Japan and China, documenting diplomatic efforts to secure flight permissions and disputes over Japanese requirements in the South Manchuria Railway Zone. The final sheet points to a related despatch by Ambassador Forbes about restrictions affecting Ford pilot Perry Hutton.

subfiles.title: List of Papers on Aerial Navigation in Japan
subfiles.about: A Department of State index identifies reports and cross-references concerning the development, regulation and geographic expansion of Japanese aviation during the 1930s.
subfiles.summary: The entries cover civil aviation reports, pilot training, aerial beacons, air-defense preparations, aircraft manufacturing and proposed or newly inaugurated routes linking Japan with China, Korea, Taiwan, Sakhalin, Southeast Asia and the South Seas Mandate. They document the consolidation of Japan Air Transport and International Air Line into Dai Nippon Air Line and the creation of a national-policy aviation company under close government control. The list also records diplomatic reporting from Japan, China, Hong Kong and Iraq and points to related records elsewhere in the State Department decimal file.

subfiles.title: List of Papers on Ford Motor Company’s Airplane Shipment to Japan
subfiles.about: This jacket-case index traces the proposed shipment and demonstration tour of a Ford airplane through Japan, China and Manchuria and the effort to obtain official flight permissions.
subfiles.summary: Ford planned to ship an airplane from Los Angeles to James H. Baer at Yokohama, accompanied by pilot Perry Hutton and mechanic Anton Hinton, for demonstrations in Japan followed by an extensive Chinese tour. The Department instructed its representatives in Tokyo and Peiping to obtain permissions, but the American Embassy reported significant Japanese obstacles to foreign aviators. Later entries concern restrictions on the aircraft’s passage through the South Manchuria Railway Zone and question Japan’s asserted authority to require special permission there.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Forbes Despatch No. 103 on Ford Flights
subfiles.about: The sheet directs researchers to a related despatch concerning requirements imposed on Perry Hutton’s Ford Motor Company flights over Japanese-controlled territory.
subfiles.summary: The note cross-references file 894.7961/7 and Despatch No. 103 from Japan, signed by Forbes and dated January 12. That despatch reportedly discusses requirements for flights over Japanese territory, the South Manchuria Railway Zone and fortified areas of the Kwantung Leased Territory in connection with Perry Hutton’s Ford demonstration flights.

interest: The bundle is valuable less for the full texts of individual reports than for the administrative map it provides of American intelligence and diplomatic reporting on Japanese aviation. Its entries show civil and military aviation developing together, with commercial routes, pilot training, manufacturing legislation and state consolidation all receiving close attention. The Ford jacket case is especially revealing: a commercial demonstration tour became a diplomatic test of sovereignty, restricted airspace and Japanese authority in Manchuria. The lists also identify reports now filed elsewhere, making them useful for reconstructing dispersed archival trails.
